books.bigTheme: Jesus the promised King of Israel
books.placeInStory: Matthew opens the New Testament by tracing Jesus back to Abraham and David, showing that the long wait of the Old Testament has reached its goal. The God who made promises to Israel now keeps every one of them in a single Galilean carpenter.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the new Moses who gives the law its true meaning and the king whose kingdom is not built on armies but on mercy. He dies, rises, and sends his followers to make disciples of all nations.

books.bigTheme: the suffering servant who is the Son of God
books.placeInStory: Mark moves fast, telling the story of Jesus as urgent news that the kingdom of God has finally arrived. It shows the moment the whole Old Testament was leaning toward, when God himself stepped into human history to rescue.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is powerful enough to still storms and cast out evil, yet he came not to be served but to give his life as a ransom for many. His path to glory runs straight through the cross.

books.bigTheme: the Savior who seeks the lost
books.placeInStory: Luke writes a careful account so an outsider can trust what happened. He shows Jesus reaching the poor, the foreigner, and the outcast, widening the old story of Israel to take in the whole world.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus comes to seek and save the lost, eating with sinners and welcoming those everyone else turned away. His compassion is the very heart of God made visible.

books.bigTheme: the eternal Word made flesh
books.placeInStory: John reaches back before Genesis to show that Jesus was with God in the beginning and is God. The light that spoke creation into being has now entered the dark world it made.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the bread, the light, the shepherd, and the resurrection, the great I AM in human skin. Whoever believes in him crosses from death into life.

books.bigTheme: the gospel spreading to the ends of the earth
books.placeInStory: Acts tells what happened after Jesus rose and returned to heaven, as the Spirit fell and the church was born. The story of one nation becomes the story of a worldwide family gathered from every tongue.
books.pointsToChrist: The risen Jesus keeps working through his people by the Holy Spirit, and his name is preached as the only one by which we are saved. What he began on earth he continues from the throne.

books.bigTheme: the righteousness of God for sinners
books.placeInStory: Paul lays out the whole plan of salvation, from human sin going back to Adam, to rescue in Christ, to the future of Israel and the nations. It explains how a holy God can welcome guilty people without ceasing to be just.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus took the judgment we earned so that we are counted right with God through faith alone. Nothing can separate those who are his from the love of God in Christ.

books.bigTheme: the cross shaping a divided church
books.placeInStory: A young church in a proud city is tearing itself apart over status, sex, and showmanship. Paul writes to show that the new community of Christ must live by a wisdom the world calls foolish.
books.pointsToChrist: Christ crucified is the power and wisdom of God, and his resurrection guarantees ours. The love that bears all things flows from him.

books.bigTheme: power made perfect in weakness
books.placeInStory: Paul defends his ministry to a church that has started doubting him, opening his own suffering for them to see. He shows that the new covenant comes through cracked and ordinary vessels.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus became poor so that we through his poverty might become rich, and his grace is enough for the weak. In him every promise of God finds its yes.

books.bigTheme: saved by grace, not by rules
books.placeInStory: Churches are being told they must add the old law to faith in Christ to truly belong to God. Paul fights for the freedom won at the cross and the promise first given to Abraham.
books.pointsToChrist: Christ became a curse for us to redeem us from the law, so that we receive the Spirit by faith. We no longer live, but Christ lives in us.

books.bigTheme: one new people united in Christ
books.placeInStory: Paul lifts the eyes of ordinary believers to God's plan from before the world was made, to gather everything in heaven and earth under one head. The ancient wall between Jew and Gentile comes down in the church.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the cornerstone who makes enemies into one body and seats us with himself in the heavenly places. By grace we are saved through faith, his gift and not our doing.

books.bigTheme: joy that holds in any circumstance
books.placeInStory: Writing from prison, Paul thanks a beloved church and urges them toward unity and steady gladness. He shows that life in Christ produces joy that chains cannot reach.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus emptied himself, took the form of a servant, and obeyed even to death, so God has given him the name above every name. To live is Christ and to die is gain.

books.bigTheme: the supremacy of Christ over all
books.placeInStory: A church is being lured toward strange teachings that add rituals and angels to Jesus. Paul answers that Christ alone is enough because everything was made by him and for him.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the image of the invisible God in whom all the fullness of God dwells, and in him we are complete. He holds all things together and reconciles all things by his blood.

books.bigTheme: living in hope of Christ's return
books.placeInStory: Paul encourages new believers under pressure to keep trusting and keep loving while they wait. He points them forward to the day the Lord will come back for his own.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus will descend from heaven and gather living and dead believers to be with him forever. Those who grieve do so in real hope because he rose.

books.bigTheme: steadfastness until the Lord comes
books.placeInStory: Some have grown confused and idle, thinking the day of the Lord has already come. Paul steadies them, correcting the error and calling them to keep working and standing firm.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus will be revealed from heaven to bring justice and relief to his suffering people. He is the one who establishes and guards our hearts until then.

books.bigTheme: how the household of God should live
books.placeInStory: Paul guides a young pastor in caring for a church, choosing leaders, and guarding sound teaching. He shows what the family of God looks like when it is healthy.
books.pointsToChrist: There is one mediator between God and people, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all. He came into the world to save sinners.

books.bigTheme: faithful to the end
books.placeInStory: Near death, Paul writes a last charge to his closest helper to hold fast and pass on the message. It is the voice of a man finishing well and handing on the trust.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel. He remains faithful even when we falter.

books.bigTheme: grace that teaches us to live
books.placeInStory: Paul tells a coworker how to set struggling churches in order and appoint trustworthy leaders. He shows that right belief and good lives belong together.
books.pointsToChrist: The grace of God appeared in Jesus, who gave himself to purify a people of his own who are eager to do good. We wait for his glorious appearing.

books.bigTheme: reconciliation in the family of Christ
books.placeInStory: Paul asks a Christian master to welcome back a runaway slave, now a brother in the faith. It is a small letter showing how the gospel reshapes real relationships.
books.pointsToChrist: Paul offers to pay the debt himself, a living picture of how Christ takes our debt and credits us to God. In Christ a slave becomes a beloved brother.

books.bigTheme: Jesus greater than everything before
books.placeInStory: Written to believers tempted to drift back to the old ways of worship, Hebrews shows that the whole system of priests and sacrifices was a shadow pointing ahead. Now the reality has come.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the great high priest who offered himself once for all and sat down, a single sacrifice that the old ones could only foreshadow. He is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

books.bigTheme: faith that proves itself in action
books.placeInStory: James writes to scattered believers about the daily shape of real trust, in how they speak, work, and treat the poor. He echoes the wisdom of the Old Testament now lived under Christ.
books.pointsToChrist: Following the Lord Jesus means a faith that works, caring for the weak and bridling the tongue. Saving faith always leaves fingerprints.

books.bigTheme: hope for a suffering church
books.placeInStory: Peter writes to believers treated as strangers and outsiders, scattered and pressed by a hostile world. He names them the new chosen people, heirs of Israel's calling.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus suffered for us, bore our sins in his body on the tree, and rose to give us a living hope. By his wounds we are healed.

books.bigTheme: guarding truth against false teachers
books.placeInStory: Peter warns a church against teachers who twist the message and mock the promise of Christ's return. He calls believers to grow and to hold the certain word.
books.pointsToChrist: The Lord is not slow about his promise but patient, not willing that any should perish. Jesus will return, and a new heaven and earth are coming.

books.bigTheme: knowing you belong to God
books.placeInStory: John writes so that believers shaken by false teaching can be sure they have eternal life. He brings the tests of true faith down to love, truth, and obedience.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the real flesh-and-blood Son who is the sacrifice for our sins, and God is love because he sent him. If we confess our sins, he is faithful to forgive.

books.bigTheme: walking in love and truth
books.placeInStory: A short letter to a church warning against deceivers who deny that Jesus came in the flesh. John guards the little flock from welcoming what would destroy it.
books.pointsToChrist: Holding to the teaching of Christ means confessing the real Jesus and loving one another. To abandon that teaching is to lose God.

books.bigTheme: supporting those who serve the truth
books.placeInStory: John commends a faithful host and rebukes a proud man who refused traveling teachers. It shows how an early church practiced welcome and care.
books.pointsToChrist: Working together for the truth means imitating good and not evil, for the one who does good belongs to God. Faithful service honors the name of Jesus.

books.bigTheme: contending for the faith
books.placeInStory: Jude urges believers to fight for the message handed down once for all, against those who twist grace into a license to sin. He draws on the warnings of the Old Testament.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is able to keep us from stumbling and present us blameless before God with great joy. We are kept for him and called to keep ourselves in his love.

books.bigTheme: the final victory of the Lamb
books.placeInStory: Revelation pulls back the curtain on history to show who really sits on the throne while the church suffers. It gathers every thread of the whole Bible and ties them off in the end God always intended.
books.pointsToChrist: Jesus is the Lamb who was slain and now reigns, the beginning and the end, who will wipe away every tear. He is making all things new and dwelling with his people forever.
